newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end shortend session weaker.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end shortend session weaker.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei stock index futures ended its shortened pre-holiday session weaker on Monday in line with Tokyo stock prices and weak technicals, dealers said.
Japanese stock prices demonstrated more volatility, worsened by the slide in the yen against the dollar, which added to the downward bias for Nikkei futures.
The key March Nikkei contract closed at 19,345, down 50 points from Friday, but off the session's low at 19,095.
Volume was dominated mostly by Japanese customers squaring positions on the last day of trade for the year. Markets in Japan are closing one day earlier this year for the New Year holiday.
"Japanese customers were trading. They came in to sell anything above 19,400," a European commission house dealer said.
But many did not take profit at lower levels, on anticipation of even further weakness when the market reopens for trade.

The Nikkei was seen vulnerable to more selling from overseas liquidation of Japanese stocks, and also the yen's tumble to 116 against the dollar. Dealers said it would probably test 18,500 points, the midpoint of a technical wave next week.
SIMEX Nikkei futures will resume trading next Monday when Tokyo markets reopen after a one week holiday.
